notes: Santería forms in western Cuba from Yoruba religion, Roman Catholicism and Spiritism, in the early houses of the cities.
Cuba becomes a republic in 1898 with freedom of religion, but Santería is marginalised and campaigns are launched against it through the first half of the 20th century.
Urban-to-rural migration has spread the religion across Cuba, and it probably reaches Santiago de Cuba in the 1930s.
Lachatañeré's Manuel de santería (1942) treats it as a religion and promotes the name Santería.
After the Revolution of 1959 practitioners face police harassment, and emigration spreads Santería to the United States, Puerto Rico, Mexico, Colombia and Venezuela.
The Ooni of Ife visits Cuba in 1987, and links grow with Yoruba religion and with Vodou and Candomblé.
Cuba is declared secular in 1992, and Santería begins to be practised more openly.
